pages.text: "Hey, noisy! Go away!" Bami shouted out the sleeping-car window. Pipi had sung there all morning. Pipi shouted right back, "Hey, noisy! Go away!"
"Don't copy me, annoying sparrow!" Bami thumped the window with their beak. Pipi replied, "Don't copy me, annoying owl!" Tears stung Bami's eyes. "I wanted to play together... Why call me annoying?"
Pipi flew behind the chimney. Pink flowering trees passed the dining-car window, but Bami was alone. "Pipi... the flowers are blooming..." Their voice grew small.
Mom set down lunchboxes and sat beside Bami. "Pipi's like an echo, returning your words. How does 'annoying owl' feel?" Bami thought. "It hurts... Then Pipi felt hurt, too."
Mom smiled. "Kind words, kind echoes! Instead of 'Noisy,' try 'What a lovely song.' Instead of 'Go away,' try 'Let's look together.'" Bami practiced softly.
At a station, Bami flew through the round window to the roof. Pipi crouched behind the chimney. Bami approached gently. "I'm sorry about before. Your song is lovely!"
Pipi peeked out and repeated, "I'm sorry about before, Bami! Your song's lovely, too!" Morning singing began again. Bami spread their wings on the roof. "Kind words, kind echoes!"
They sat side by side, looking at pink blossoms. "Let's look together, Pipi!" "Let's look together, Bami!" Every kind word opened Bami's heart like a flower.
That evening, Bami counted for Pipi. "One, pause before speaking! Two, choose kind words! Three, remember thank you and sorry!" When Mom packed their lunch, Bami spoke first. "Thank you!"
Mom wrapped Bami in her apron. "Kind words brought Pipi's song back!" Kind words came back as kind words. Kind words, kind echoes! Pipi chirped along from the roof.
